newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares down at noon, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares down at noon, trade thin.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B shares edged lower at midday on Thursday, with few investors willing to take new positions in the absence of fresh factors, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.38 point or 0.29 percent to 129.66. Turnover was a thin HK$5.8 milliion.
The domestic A share index gained 0.53 point or 0.13 percent to 408.26 on turnover of 2.2 billion yuan.
"The (B share) market is somewhat forgotten by investors," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. "Few investors are building new positions, while few are willing to sell," she added.
"The B share index is still trending downwards, but any sharp falls are unlikely," the analyst said.
The market is still waiting for major market-moving news, such as better-than-expected interim results, to stimulate trade, a second China Guotai analyst said.
Beverage maker Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co was the biggest B share loser, falling HK$0.19 or 5.60 percent to HK$3.20 on volume of 2,500 shares.
Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded issue, gaining HK$0.01 to HK$2.01 on volume of 611,500 shares.

Shijiazhuang Petrochemical Co Ltd 0783.SZ, a refinery that listed 108 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, closed the morning at 10.10 yuan against issue price of 5.89 yuan a share. Volume reached 46 million shares, making it the most actively traded issue.
